newsitem.title: USA: Clinton will meet Republicans "half way" on budget.
newsitem.headline: Clinton will meet Republicans "half way" on budget.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Thursday that his fiscal year 1998 budget proposal would balance the budget by the year 2002 and that he would meet the Republicans "half way" on reaching that goal.

"I think this budget will show that I am making a clear effort to reach out to them and meet them half way to get this job done," Clinton told reporters in a White House event to announce a drop in student loan default rates.
"I also expect there to be a negotiating process with the Congress, and I will work with them in good faith as have said all along," Clinton said.

Asked if he had made all his final budget decisions and if there were any chance of reopening them, specifically on the Medicare health care program for the elderly, Clinton said: "I have completed some time ago the work on the budget. We still ...have to work around the edges from time to time."
Clinton also said he was confident it would be possible to reach a balanced budget under Office of Management and Budget (OMB) or Congressional Budget Office economic assumptions.
"I also am pleased that the OMB and the Congressional Budget Office have been working together to try to narrow together the gap between all these assumptions they have," he added.

Clinton strongly defended the education tax cut proposals that he made during the presidential election and said that he believes the atmosphere between the White House and the Republican-controlled Congress is good.

"If the atmosphere of this Congress reflects what happened in the last two months of the last Congress, I think the American people will get their balanced budget," Clinton said. "They will get these education tax credits, they will get the next step of welfare reform ... It will be a very, very good time. The atmopshere so far feels good to me."
